questions.q: How did the Rangoon compare with the Mongolia?
choices: It was slower but much more comfortable
It was as fast but not as well fitted up
It was bigger, faster and more luxurious
It was smaller and had no cabins for ladies
questions.evidence: She was as fast, but not as well fitted up, as the Mongolia

questions.q: How did Mr. Fogg behave toward Aouda on the voyage?
choices: He talked to her for hours about his travels and his club
He avoided her and stayed alone playing whist all day
He seemed cold, but made sure she had everything she needed
He was cheerful and joked with her at every meal
questions.evidence: he seemed to be always on the watch that nothing should be wanting to Aouda's comfort

questions.q: Fogg treated Aouda "with the precision of an automaton." What is an automaton?
choices: A clockwork machine
A kind and gentle nurse
A strict army officer
A court judge in a wig
questions.evidence: with the precision of an automaton

questions.q: Whom did Aouda hope to join in Hong Kong?
choices: Her uncle, an officer in the English army
Jeejeeh, a cousin of a rich Parsee baronet
Sir Francis Cromarty's married sister
An old school friend from her days in Bombay
questions.evidence: it was his cousin, Jeejeeh, whom she hoped to join at Hong Kong

questions.q: Why did Fix think the arrest had to happen in Hong Kong?
choices: It was the last English ground; beyond it a simple warrant would be useless
The judge in Hong Kong was an old friend who owed him a favour
Fogg had told Passepartout that he planned to stay there for a whole month or more
His own money would run out before the ship reached Japan
questions.evidence: Hong Kong was the last English ground on which he would set foot

questions.q: Why was telling Passepartout the truth a dangerous plan for Fix?
choices: Passepartout might attack him with his fists
One word from Passepartout to his master would ruin everything
The captain would surely put him off the ship when it reached Singapore
Aouda would warn the police in Hong Kong first
questions.evidence: A word from Passepartout to his master would ruin all.

questions.q: What new idea did Aouda's presence give Fix?
choices: That Fogg might have run off with her, which could be used to stop him
That she was a detective sent from Bombay to help him
That she might know exactly where Fogg had hidden the rest of the stolen bank money
That she would pay Fix to protect her from the priests
questions.evidence: He asked himself whether there had not been a wicked elopement

questions.q: From Singapore, how could Fix warn the authorities in Hong Kong?
choices: By sending a letter on a faster mail steamer
By the telegraph wire
By asking the captain to signal with flags
By sending a messenger on a fishing boat
questions.evidence: there is a telegraphic wire to Hong Kong

questions.q: How did Fix act when he finally met Passepartout on deck?
choices: He acted very surprised to see him
He hid his face and walked quickly away
He told him at once that he was a detective
He asked to speak to Mr. Fogg in private
questions.evidence: with every appearance of extreme surprise

questions.q: What excuse did Fix give for not being seen since Calcutta?
choices: He had been busy writing letters for the company
He had been sea-sick and stayed in his berth
He had come on board only at the last port
He had been helping the captain on the bridge
questions.evidence: Oh, a trifle of sea-sickness--I've been staying in my berth.

questions.q: Why was Fix disappointed to learn Aouda would stay with a relative in Hong Kong?
choices: It meant there was no elopement he could use against Fogg
It meant Fogg would have to stay in Hong Kong for a long time
It meant Passepartout would leave the ship with her
It meant she could not help him find the stolen money

questions.q: What is this chapter mostly about?
choices: Aouda and Fogg exploring the Andaman Islands on foot
Fix planning how to stop Fogg and meeting Passepartout again
Passepartout learning that Fix is really a detective
A storm that nearly sinks the Rangoon near Singapore
questions.evidence: Fix prepared to make himself known
